newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech to file in Michigan in next few weeks.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech to file in Michigan in next few weeks.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Tuesday it plans on refiling soon its application to provide long-distance telephone service in Michigan.

Richard Notebaert, chairman and chief executive of Ameritech, told reporters at a monthly briefing that the company expects to refile "over the next few weeks", citing a recent interconnection agreement for the state between the company and long-distance provider AT&T Corp.

On January 2, Ameritech became the first Baby Bell to ask the U.S. Federal Communications Commission for permission to enter the Michigan market when it filed to offer long-distance telephone service to residents of the state.
But it was forced to withdraw that application in February after the FCC said the documents were flawed.

AT&T said Monday it had filed a tariff with the Michigan Public Service Commission to begin providing local service. When Ameritech withdrew its earlier application, the FCC said Ameritech had not submitted a finalized agreement showing it opened its local phone network to competition.

Notebaert said he was hesitant to project when Ameritech would file to provide long-distance in the other four Midwestern states in which it provides local service, citing procedural issues. He said, however, the company hopes to have filed in all states by the end of the year.
"It's too slow," Notebaert said of the regulatory review procedure, adding that competition and technology are both changing quickly.
He said "we have to find a way to do things quicker," without compromising the integrity of the governmental review.

Under last year's Telecommunications Act, regional telephone companies must prove to regulators that their local monopolies are open to competition before gaining access to the $80 billion long-distance market.
